reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: § 14.2 grants a revocable, non-transferable, Order-Form-term licence to Deliverables with no mention of Affiliates or contractors, which is the rule's walk-away position, and it contradicts the perpetual/irrevocable paid-up bargain in §§ 13.2–13.3.

The redline reaches the preferred position: it names Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf, makes the licence perpetual and irrevocable, allows transfer to an Affiliate or successor, and limits revocation to § 13.3 (material uncured breach after notice and cure).
Vendor's exclusive ownership of Deliverables is preserved, so the edit is confined to the licence grant and does not overreach into IP ownership.

The failed minimality check (0.838 changed-character ratio) is explained by the fact that every operative element of the original sentence (revocable, non-transferable, term-limited, silent on Affiliates) had to be replaced; the rewrite mirrors the already-agreed § 13.2 language rather than inventing new terms.
Comment is accurate, cites the playbook position and the internal § 13.2/13.3 inconsistency, offers the M&A-successor fallback, and matches the required prefix and tone.

Minor point only: the grant adds modify/derivative-work rights that the rule does not strictly require; this is defensible as a mirror of § 13.2 but is the likeliest target for counterparty pushback and could be dropped if resistance arises.
